data.narrative:
Vertical Aerospace is a public-stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector founded by Stephen Fitzpatrick, having raised $50M to date. The relevant peer universe consists of eight private companies operating in the same sector, including Joby Aviation, Archer Aviation, Waymo, Wayve, and Zipline. No public comparables exist within this narrow segment, limiting the applicability of traditional public market benchmarking.

Peer-median valuation analysis was not applicable in this case. The Drones & Autonomous sector contains only two same-stage peers and zero companies at adjacent stages or within similar valuation tiers, falling short of the three-datapoint minimum required for reliable triangulation. A broader all-sector median would introduce material distortion given the heterogeneity of autonomous vehicle and drone business models, regulatory pathways, and commercialization timelines across the peer set.

Without sufficient narrow-peer data, traditional comparable company analysis cannot be responsibly applied. A complete valuation framework would require supplementary methods—such as discounted cash flow analysis using company-specific unit economics, venture capital method benchmarking against typical Series round multiples in autonomous systems, or precedent transaction analysis within the sector. The scarcity of public comps and limited same-stage private precedents reflects the early and fragmented nature of commercial drone and autonomous vehicle markets. Valuation confidence is inherently constrained by data limitations rather than fundamental company metrics.
